title: High Throughput Traction Force Microscopy Using PDMS Reveals Dose-Dependent Effects of Transforming Growth Factor-β on the Epithelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition
protocol: Mix Part A and Part B of PDMS kit in a 1:1 weight ratio into the 50 mL tube.
Add the required amount of curing agent for the desired modulus of the substrate.
Mix the formulation on the rotator for 30-45 min at a speed slow enough to ensure thorough mixing.
Clean the glass slide with ethanol or isopropanol.
Dry the glass slide with a lint-free wipe.
Place the cleaned and dried glass slide in the custom-built chuck on the spin-coater.
Turn on the vacuum to hold the glass slide in place.
Apply uncured PDMS approximately 1 cm from the edges of the glass slide and work towards the center.
Apply enough (3-4 mL) PDMS to ensure full coverage of the surface.
Accelerate the spin-coater from 0 to 200 rpm at 50 rpm/s.
Hold the spin-coater at 200 rpm for 1 minute.
Accelerate the spin-coater from 200 to 300 rpm at 50 rpm/s.
Hold the spin-coater at 300 rpm for 1 minute.
Decelerate the spin-coater to 0 rpm at 50 rpm/s.
Place the coated slide in an oven at 100 °C for 2 hours.
Resuspend synthesized fiduciary beads in hexane and sonicate.
Filter the bead suspension through a 5 μm syringe filter (optional).
Take out the slide from the oven, allow it to cool to room temperature, and place it on the spin-coater.
Add 3-4 ml of the bead and uncured PDMS mixture onto the surface of the coated sample.
Spin the sample starting from 0 to 500 rpm at an acceleration of 100 rpm/s.
Hold the spin speed at 500 rpm for 1 minute.
Accelerate the spin from 500 to 5000 rpm at 200 rpm/s.
Hold the spin speed at 5000 rpm for 10 seconds.
Decelerate the sample to 0 rpm at a deceleration of 100 rpm/s.
Disable the vacuum and remove the coated slide without touching the coated surface.
Place the spin-coated sample in an oven set to 100 °C for 1 hour.
Add Part A (base) and Part B (curing agent, e.g., Sylgard) of a PDMS elastomer kit in a 10:1 weight ratio into a 50 mL tube.
Mix the mixture on a rotator for 30-45 minutes.
Apply the mixture to the bottom of the divider and spread it evenly.
Lay the substrate onto the divider upside-down.
Place the sample upside-down in an oven at 65 °C for 2 hours.
Take out samples from the oven.
Clean the bottom of the glass with 70% ethanol or isopropanol.
Dissolve 80 μL of a Sulfo-SANPAH aliquot in 40 mL of 0.1 M HEPES buffer (pH 7-9).
Add 200 μL of diluted Sulfo-SANPAH solution to each well of the 96-well plate.
Expose the plate to UV light at a distance of 5 cm for 10-15 min.
Remove the Sulfo-SANPAH solution from the wells.
Add 200 μL of 5 µg/mL fibronectin solution to each well.
Incubate the plate at 4 °C overnight.
Remove the fibronectin solution and wash each well with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) twice.
Add 200 µL of PBS to each well.
Place a lid on the sample.
Sterilize the sample under UV light in a biological safety cabinet for 30 min.
Remove PBS from each well and add 200 µL of cells suspended in culture media to each well.
Plate the cells at the desired cell density.
Prepare the complete growth culture media for NMuMG cells by supplementing DMEM with 5% FBS, 10 mM HEPES, 10 µg/mL insulin, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 1 mM L-glutamine, and 0.5 µg/mL amphotericin B.
Reconstitute insulin stock by mixing in acidified water (2.5 mL of glacial acetic acid in 130 mL of deionized water) to a concentration of 10 mg/mL.
Store the insulin stock solution at 4 °C until clear, then filter through a 0.22 µm pore filter.
Dissolve 2 µg of TGF-β in 100 µL of 10 mM citric acid (pH 3.0) to prepare the TGF-β stock solution.
Vortex the tube containing the TGF-β stock and aliquot into desired volumes.
Store the TGF-β aliquots at -80 °C.
Add 1.5 µL of TGF-β stock solution to 10 mL of complete cell culture media to achieve a final TGF-β concentration of 3 ng/mL.
Acquire at least one image of fiduciary particles and cells for each position.
Focus on the bead layer in the acquired images.
Optimize pixel size based on the size of the fiduciary particles and image processing method.
Use a 10x 0.4 NA objective to acquire images with 1024 x 1024 resolution.
Ensure a resolution of at least approximately 1-5 pixels per bead, considering the individual size range of 300-500 nm for polydisperse beads.
Prioritize focus and imaging quality of fluorescent fiduciary beads over cells themselves.
Ensure no cross-talk between different channels in the images, particularly avoiding fluorescence not from the fiduciary beads.
Add detachment solution to each well after recording positions of interest to acquire force-free reference images of the fiduciary particles.
Prepare cell detachment solution by mixing an aqueous solution containing 2% TritonX-100, 50 mM sodium azide, and 500 mM potassium hydroxide.
Set up the three-neck flask with a water-cooled reflux condenser under a fume hood.
Equip one neck of the flask with a rubber septum for nitrogen inlet and outlet needles, and another neck for reagent addition using a syringe.
Add 0.5 mL of PDMS stabilizer and fluorophore to the flask.
Purge the flask with nitrogen gas for 1 hour under continuous stirring at 75°C.
Add 100 mL of anhydrous hexane to the flask along with a small magnetic stir bar.
Add 6 mL of methylmethacrylate to a round bottom flask and purify it by flushing through a pre-packed column.
Add 0.100 g of AIBN to the purified methylmethacrylate in the round-bottom flask, then purge this mixture with nitrogen gas for 1 hour.
Transfer the AIBN-methylmethacrylate mixture into the three-neck flask containing hexane and stabilizer.
Stir the mixture until it becomes cloudy, indicating the start of polymerization.
Continue stirring the solution for an additional 3 hours after it turns cloudy.
Cool the reaction mixture to room temperature by placing the flask in an ice water bath.
Vacuum-filter the cooled solution using coarse filter paper.
Centrifuge the filtrate and re-suspend the particles in hexane.
Initialize the system and calibrate the device and measuring system (parallel plate, d = 25 mm).
Measure the zero gap.
Load the PDMS sample onto the bottom plate of rheometer.
Move the spindle down to completely contact the top of the PDMS sample.
Trim the loaded sample excess from the bottom plate.
In a strain sweep test, apply increasing strains for each composition with different crosslinking density.
Ensure the polymer structure remains in the linear viscoelastic regime during all shear measurements.
Measure the dynamic shear storage modulus (G') and loss modulus (G′′) of the PDMS network.
Conduct the measurement in a time sweep test at a frequency of 1 Hz and oscillatory shear strain of 0.5% at 100 °C.
Apply a frequency sweep test with a frequency ranging from 0.1-100 Hz.
Maintain an oscillatory shear strain of 0.5% during the frequency sweep test.
